question: A 5-year-old with a 6-month history of painful defecation, only 1 bowel motion every 5–7 days, and foul-smelling faecal soiling is diagnosed with functional constipation. Abdominal examination confirms a loaded rectum. Which management step should PRECEDE maintenance laxative therapy?

answers.text: Start dietary fibre supplementation alone and review in 4 weeks.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Dietary advice is part of management but is insufficient alone when a faecal impaction is present. Impaction must be cleared before a maintenance laxative can work effectively.

answers.text: Perform a disimpaction course using polyethylene glycol (PEG/macrogol) before starting maintenance therapy.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Per ESPGHAN guidelines, when faecal impaction is present, disimpaction (oral high-dose PEG or rectal enemas if oral not tolerated) must precede maintenance laxative therapy. PEG/macrogol is the first-line agent. Maintenance therapy (lower-dose PEG ± lactulose) follows.

answers.text: Perform a barium enema immediately to rule out Hirschsprung disease.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A barium enema is not the first step when the clinical picture fits functional constipation in a 5-year-old with a loaded rectum. Imaging is reserved for atypical features suggesting organic disease (e.g. empty rectum, failure to pass meconium at birth, ribbon stools, neurological signs).

answers.text: Order a full-thickness rectal biopsy as the definitive investigation before initiating any treatment.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Rectal biopsy is reserved for cases where Hirschsprung disease is strongly suspected clinically. A 5-year-old with a loaded rectum, faecal soiling, and ROME IV-consistent history = functional constipation; begin treatment without biopsy.

overallFeedback.feedback: When impaction is present, disimpaction must come first. Maintenance laxatives (PEG, lactulose) without clearing the impaction are ineffective. Hirschsprung disease is unlikely in a 5-year-old with a loaded rectum and typical functional history.

Correct. The key step is disimpaction before maintenance. PEG/macrogol (oral) is the preferred agent. ESPGHAN guidelines guide the step-wise approach: education + disimpaction + maintenance laxatives + toilet training.
